# Warning Thresholds

A tsunami warning is issued when an offshore earthquake of sufficient
magnitude is detected near a coastline. Coastal communities should treat any
strong or prolonged ground shaking near the coast as a natural warning sign,
independent of an official alert, and move to higher ground immediately.

## Evacuation

Evacuate on foot where possible. Vehicles create congestion that can trap
people in low-lying areas. Move to designated vertical evacuation structures
or high ground at least thirty metres above sea level or several kilometres
inland, whichever is reached first.

# Coastal Infrastructure

Critical facilities sited near the coast — hospitals, ports, power
generation — should maintain documented evacuation and shutdown procedures
that do not depend on grid power, since a tsunami-generating event may also
disrupt electrical supply.
